$comment: Second half of the injection pair. `fast-element-html.injection.json` opens the template and hands its body to text.html.basic / source.css; from there the body is tokenized by rules those grammars pushed, and a pattern listed on our own begin/end rule is never consulted again — so ${…} inside a tag or a declaration block, and FAST's :/?/@ prefixed attributes, need an injection that fires at any depth. The selectors match only inside our own templates (string.template.fast-element.ts). They deliberately carry no `-meta.embedded.line.ts`: a template nested in an interpolation of another one sits *under* a `meta.embedded.line.ts`, so excluding interpolations would leave every nested body without its ${…} and its bindings, and a scope selector has no way to say “the innermost embedded marker is the html one”. Firing inside plain interpolations too costs nothing: `templateInterpolation` only repeats what source.ts would have done for the same ${…}, and a binding pattern needs a `:name="` that no TypeScript expression spells. A binding rule has to swallow the whole attribute, value and all: text.html.basic does not recognise a :/?/@ name, so anything we leave behind lands on its `invalid.illegal.character-not-allowed-here` catch-all.
